Primary Care Progress Note
Date: 08/13/2026
Patient: Michell VonRueden, 86-year-old female

Subjective:
Ms. VonRueden presents for her routine follow-up visit. She reports feeling generally well with no new complaints today. She denies any recent falls or injuries.

Objective:
Vital signs are stable and within normal limits. Physical examination reveals no acute distress. Cardiovascular, respiratory, and abdominal exams are unremarkable. Musculoskeletal exam shows no tenderness or swelling.

Assessment:
Ms. VonRueden is an elderly female with stable health status at this time. No new concerns noted.

Plan:
Continue current management and routine monitoring. Encourage regular physical activity and balanced nutrition. Follow up as scheduled or sooner if any new symptoms arise.

Radiology Report
Date: 09/08/2026
Patient: Michell VonRueden, 86-year-old female

Examination: MRI thoracolumbar spine

Findings:
MRI thoracolumbar spine 09/08/2026: acute osteoporotic T11 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging.

Impression:
There is evidence of an acute osteoporotic compression fracture at the T11 vertebral level, characterized by bone marrow edema visible on STIR sequences. No additional acute abnormalities are identified.

Recommendations:
Clinical correlation is advised. Follow-up imaging may be considered based on clinical presentation and management needs.

notes.text:
Spine Intervention Consultation
Date: 09/10/2026
Patient: Michell VonRueden, 86-year-old female

History:
Back pain began 08/07/2026 after a fall from standing height, 5 weeks before this visit. Seen in the outpatient spine clinic; not hospitalized for this fracture. Pain NRS 8/10 despite 4 weeks of optimal non-surgical management with oxycodone 5 mg as needed, a thoracolumbar brace and activity modification. Pain has worsened over the past two weeks despite bracing.

Clinical Findings:
Back pain localizes to the fractured level; afebrile with no signs of infection or discitis.

Plan:
Referred for DEXA bone density testing and osteoporosis education; enrolled in the osteoporosis treatment program. Continue current pain management and bracing. Consider interventional options based on clinical progression and imaging findings.
